cases.reason: Ordinary complex skein gluing is bilinear, so the current definition contradicts its conjugate-linearity assertion (B(empty,i empty)=iη rather than−iη). BHMV1.9 actually uses same-oriented-boundary fillings and reverses the second. The proposal explicitly makes that semilinear reversal part of the construction and aligns the directly affected pairing lemma.

literal_replacements.source_excerpt: Fix a marked handlebody $H$ with boundary $\Sigma$ and a complementary marked handlebody $H'$ so that their oriented gluing is the standard $S^3$; the boundary bands on $H$ and $H'$ are identified by the marking, with labels dualized on the oppositely oriented side.
literal_replacements.proposed_replacement: For connected $\Sigma$, fix marked handlebodies $H,H'$ whose boundaries are both identified orientation-preservingly with $\Sigma$, so that $H\cup_\Sigma(-H')$ is the standard oriented $S^3$. Both filling modules carry the specified boundary labels before reversal; orientation reversal of the second filling dualizes its boundary labels and reverses its ribbon-end arcs. Disconnected and empty surfaces are included by the tensor and unit convention below.

literal_replacements.source_excerpt: For $x\in\mathcal K_A(H;I_\Sigma,\mathbf a)$ and $y\in\mathcal K_A(H';I_\Sigma,\mathbf a^*)$, glue their matching boundary bands and idempotents. This gives a closed colored ribbon graph $\Gamma$ in the standard $S^3$. Define the handlebody pairing by $B_\Sigma(x,y)=Z_p(S^3,\Gamma,w)$, using the normalized root surgery evaluation and the weight $w$ prescribed by the fixed Lagrangian data. This is the BHMV sesquilinear pairing: it is linear in $x$ and conjugate-linear in $y$ for the coefficient involution $A\mapsto A^{-1}$, $\kappa\mapsto\kappa^{-1}$.
literal_replacements.proposed_replacement: Let $\mathfrak r:\mathcal K_A(H';I_\Sigma,\mathbf a)\to\mathcal K_A(-H';-I_\Sigma,\mathbf a^*)$ be the semilinear orientation-reversal map: for a finite skein sum, $\mathfrak r(\sum_L c_L[L])=\sum_L\overline{c_L}[-L]$, with the second filling, its ribbon data and anomaly data reversed. The bar is complex conjugation, so $\overline A=A^{-1}$ and $\overline\kappa=\kappa^{-1}$. Reversal exchanges the two bracket smoothings, and conjugation exchanges their coefficients, so $\mathfrak r$ respects the skein relations and the boundary projectors. For $x\in\mathcal K_A(H;I_\Sigma,\mathbf a)$ and $y\in\mathcal K_A(H';I_\Sigma,\mathbf a)$, glue $x$ to $\mathfrak r(y)$ along the matching boundary bands and idempotents. Denote the resulting graph by $\Gamma(x,\mathfrak r(y))$. Define $B_\Sigma(x,y)=Z_p(S^3,\Gamma(x,\mathfrak r(y)),w)$ with the prescribed gluing weight. This is linear in $x$ and conjugate-linear in $y$, as in BHMV Proposition 1.9, p.891. Ordinary gluing of two already oppositely oriented skein inputs is instead bilinear; the reversal here is part of the Definition.

literal_replacements.source_excerpt: This is the radical-quotient handlebody state-space construction for the specified marking and anomaly data. Independence of the marking, finite generation, nondegeneracy, and the gluing maps are separate mathematical obligations.
literal_replacements.proposed_replacement: This is the radical-quotient handlebody state-space construction for a connected marked surface. For a finite disjoint union $\Sigma=\bigsqcup_{a=1}^k\Sigma_a$ with the direct-sum component reference Lagrangian, define $V_p(\Sigma)=\bigotimes_{a=1}^kV_p(\Sigma_a)$, and define its pairing as the product of the component sesquilinear pairings on pure tensors. Set $V_p(\varnothing)=\mathbb C$ and $B_\varnothing(z,w)=z\overline w$. Permuting components uses the ordinary tensor symmetry; the empty tensor is the unit. These are the external BHMV conventions (Q1) p.885 and (M) p.886, whose validity for even $p\ge4$ is part of Theorem 1.4 p.887; Gilmer–Masbaum §11 p.24 also states the empty-surface unit. For an arbitrary specified real Lagrangian, including one that does not split over components, use the weight-zero identity cylinder from the componentwise handlebody-kernel reference to that Lagrangian in the registered weighted theory. The reverse cylinder is its inverse since $\mu(L,L',L)=0$, exactly as in the existing real-reference transport for weighted gluing; this does not assume every real Lagrangian splits or is rational. The tensor conventions are taken at the reference objects and then transported by these inverse cylinders. Independence of the marking, finite generation, nondegeneracy and the gluing maps remain separate mathematical obligations supplied below by the stated external BHMV/weighted theory inputs.
